source.text: Φοβήθητι, φησί, τὸν Κύριον καὶ φύλασσε τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ· φυλάσσων οὖν τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἔσῃ δυνατὸς ἐν πάσῃ πράξει, καὶ ἡ πρᾶξίς σου ἀσύγκριτος ἔσται. φοβούμενος γὰρ τὸν Κύριον πάντα καλῶς ἐργάσῃ· οὗτος δέ ἐστιν ὁ φόβος, ὃν δεῖ σε φοβηθῆναι καὶ σωθήσῃ. 2. τὸν δὲ διάβολον μὴ φοβηθῇς· φοβούμενος γὰρ τὸν Κύριον κατακυριεύσεις τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι δύναμις ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν. ἐν ᾧ [δὲ] δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐδὲ φόβος· ἐν ᾧ δὲ δύναμις ᾖ ἔνδοξος, καὶ φόβος ἐν αὐτῷ. πᾶς γὰρ ὁ δύναμιν ἔχων φόβον ἔχει· ὁ δὲ μὴ ἔχων δύναμιν ὑπὸ πάντων καταφρονεῖται. 3. φοβήθητι δὲ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι πονηρά ἐστι. φοβούμενος οὖν τὸν Κύριον φοβηθήσῃ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, καὶ οὐκ ἐργάσῃ αὐτά, ἀλλ᾽ ἀφέξῃ ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν. 4. δισσοὶ οὖν εἰσὶν οἱ φόβοι· ἐὰν γὰρ θέλῃς τὸ πονηρὸν ἐργάσασθαι, φοβοῦ τὸν Κύριον καὶ οὐκ ἐργάσῃ αὐτό· ἐὰν δὲ θέλῃς πάλιν τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐργάσασθαι, φοβοῦ τὸν Κύριον καὶ ἐργάσῃ αὐτό. ὥστε ὁ φόβος τοῦ Κυρίου ἰσχυρός ἐστι καὶ μέγας καὶ ἔνδοξος. φοβήθητι οὖν τὸν Κύριον, καὶ ζήσῃ αὐτῷ· καὶ ὅσοι ἂν φοβηθῶσιν αὐτὸν τῶν φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ζήσονται τῷ Θεῷ. 5. Διατί, φημί, κύριε, εἶπας περὶ τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ· Ζήσονται τῷ Θεῷ; Ὅτι, φησί, πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις φοβεῖται τὸν Κύριον, τὰς δὲ ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ οὐ φυλάσσει. τῶν οὖν φοβουμένων αὐτὸν καὶ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ἐκείνων ἡ ζωή ἐστι παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ· τῶν δὲ μὴ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ ζωὴ ἐν αὐτῷ.
source.label: Mandate 7

translation.text:
1. “Fear,” he says, “the Lord, and keep his commandments. By keeping the commandments of God you will be powerful in every deed, and your conduct will be beyond compare. For in fearing the Lord you will do everything well. This is the fear that you must have—and you will be saved.

2. But do not fear the devil; for by fearing the Lord you will gain mastery over the devil, because there is no power in him. In the one who has no power, there is no fear; but in the one who has glorious power, there is also fear. For everyone who has power is feared, but the one who has no power is despised by all.

3. But fear the works of the devil, for they are evil. So, by fearing the Lord, you will fear the works of the devil, and you will not do them, but will keep away from them.

4. Therefore there are two fears: if you wish to do what is evil, fear the Lord and you will not do it; and if, on the other hand, you wish to do what is good, fear the Lord and you will do it. Thus the fear of the Lord is strong and great and glorious. So fear the Lord, and you will live for him; and all who fear him among those who keep his commandments will live for God.

5. “Why,” I said, “sir, did you say about those who keep his commandments, ‘They will live for God’?” “Because,” he said, “all creation fears the Lord, but it does not keep his commandments. Therefore the life of those who fear him and keep his commandments is with God; but for those who do not keep his commandments, there is not even life in them.”

source.text: Φοβήθητι, φησί, τὸν Κύριον καὶ φύλασσε τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ· φυλάσσων οὖν τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ Θεοῦ ἔσῃ δυνατὸς ἐν πάσῃ πράξει, καὶ ἡ πρᾶξίς σου ἀσύγκριτος ἔσται. φοβούμενος γὰρ τὸν Κύριον πάντα καλῶς ἐργάσῃ· οὗτος δέ ἐστιν ὁ φόβος, ὃν δεῖ σε φοβηθῆναι καὶ σωθήσῃ. 2. τὸν δὲ διάβολον μὴ φοβηθῇς· φοβούμενος γὰρ τὸν Κύριον κατακυριεύσεις τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι δύναμις ἐν αὐτῷ οὐκ ἔστιν. ἐν ᾧ [δὲ] δύναμις οὐκ ἔστιν, οὐδὲ φόβος· ἐν ᾧ δὲ δύναμις ᾖ ἔνδοξος, καὶ φόβος ἐν αὐτῷ. πᾶς γὰρ ὁ δύναμιν ἔχων φόβον ἔχει· ὁ δὲ μὴ ἔχων δύναμιν ὑπὸ πάντων καταφρονεῖται. 3. φοβήθητι δὲ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, ὅτι πονηρά ἐστι. φοβούμενος οὖν τὸν Κύριον φοβηθήσῃ τὰ ἔργα τοῦ διαβόλου, καὶ οὐκ ἐργάσῃ αὐτά, ἀλλ᾽ ἀφέξῃ ἀπ᾽ αὐτῶν. 4. δισσοὶ οὖν εἰσὶν οἱ φόβοι· ἐὰν γὰρ θέλῃς τὸ πονηρὸν ἐργάσασθαι, φοβοῦ τὸν Κύριον καὶ οὐκ ἐργάσῃ αὐτό· ἐὰν δὲ θέλῃς πάλιν τὸ ἀγαθὸν ἐργάσασθαι, φοβοῦ τὸν Κύριον καὶ ἐργάσῃ αὐτό. ὥστε ὁ φόβος τοῦ Κυρίου ἰσχυρός ἐστι καὶ μέγας καὶ ἔνδοξος. φοβήθητι οὖν τὸν Κύριον, καὶ ζήσῃ αὐτῷ· καὶ ὅσοι ἂν φοβηθῶσιν αὐτὸν τῶν φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ζήσονται τῷ Θεῷ. 5. Διατί, φημί, κύριε, εἶπας περὶ τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ· Ζήσονται τῷ Θεῷ; Ὅτι, φησί, πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις φοβεῖται τὸν Κύριον, τὰς δὲ ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ οὐ φυλάσσει. τῶν οὖν φοβουμένων αὐτὸν καὶ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, ἐκείνων ἡ ζωή ἐστι παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ· τῶν δὲ μὴ φυλασσόντων τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ οὐδὲ ζωὴ ἐν αὐτῷ.

translation.text: 5. “Why,” I said, “sir, did you say about those who keep his commandments, ‘They will live to God’?” “Because,” he said, “all creation fears the Lord, but it does not keep his commandments. Therefore the life of those who fear him and keep his commandments is with God; but for those who do not keep his commandments, there is not even life in them.”

base_translation.text: 1. “Fear,” he says, “the Lord, and keep his commandments. By keeping the commandments of God you will be powerful in every deed, and your conduct will be incomparable. For in fearing the Lord you will do everything well. This is the fear that you must have—and you will be saved.

translation.text: 1. He says, “Fear the Lord and obey his commandments. When you obey God’s commandments, you will have strength in everything you do, and no one will surpass the way you live. If you fear the Lord, you will do everything well. This is the kind of fear you must have, and you will be saved.”

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: God’s commands are to be faithfully followed.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Obey” states the intended action more directly in common English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: you will be powerful in every deed
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: you will have strength in everything you do
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Obedience gives the person power or strength for action.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB main text and source-driven controlling meaning
simplification_decisions.rationale: The rewrite replaces an unnatural expression while retaining its promise of strength.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: no one will surpass the way you live
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The person’s manner of life will be unsurpassed.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The comparison is recast as a clear verbal statement.

risk_flags.risk: Modern readers may understand “fear” only as terror.
risk_flags.mitigation: The biblical command “fear the Lord” is retained because the POB gives no basis for narrowing it to reverence alone.

risk_flags.risk: “No one will surpass” may sound more explicitly comparative than “incomparable.”
risk_flags.mitigation: It preserves the POB’s claim that such conduct is beyond comparison.

base_translation.text: 2. But do not fear the devil; for by fearing the Lord you will gain mastery over the devil, because there is no power in him. In one in whom there is no power, there is no fear; but in one in whom there is glorious power, there is also fear. For everyone who has power has fear, but the one who has no power is despised by all.

translation.text: 2. But do not fear the devil. If you fear the Lord, you will overcome the devil, because the devil has no power. Someone with no power is not to be feared, but someone with glorious power is to be feared. Anyone who has power is feared, while everyone despises one who has none.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: by fearing the Lord you will gain mastery over the devil
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: If you fear the Lord, you will overcome the devil
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Reverence for the Lord enables a person to prevail over the devil.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Overcome” expresses gaining mastery in familiar English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: In one in whom there is no power, there is no fear
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: Someone with no power is not to be feared
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: A powerless being gives no valid reason for fear.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The direct wording preserves the contrast while removing an awkward construction.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: the one who has no power is despised by all
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: everyone despises one who has none
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The powerless one is universally treated with contempt in this contrast.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The repetition is shortened while retaining the force of “by all.”

interpretive_expansions.pob_phrase: in one in whom there is glorious power, there is also fear
interpretive_expansions.rendering: someone with glorious power is to be feared
interpretive_expansions.claim: Fear describes the response inspired by the powerful one, not fear felt by that person.
evidence: The clause contrasts with the powerless one who is not to be feared.
The paragraph commands fear of the Lord rather than fear of the devil.

risk_flags.risk: “The devil has no power” may sound like an unrestricted doctrinal claim.
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording follows the controlling POB and remains within its contrast with the Lord’s glorious power.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: 2. But do not fear the devil. If you fear the Lord, you will overcome the devil, because the devil has no power. Someone with no power is not to be feared, but someone with glorious power is. Anyone who has power is feared, while everyone despises one who has none.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft appropriately makes “gain mastery” more familiar as “overcome” and correctly clarifies that the fear associated with glorious power is fear of that powerful one, not fear experienced by him. That clarification is warranted by the immediate contrast and the command to fear the Lord rather than the devil. However, the current wording omits the predicate in the key contrast (“someone with glorious power is”), making the sentence incomplete and less clear than the POB. Supply “to be feared.”

base_translation.text: 3. But fear the works of the devil, for they are evil. So, by fearing the Lord, you will fear the works of the devil, and you will not do them, but will keep away from them.

translation.text: 3. But fear the devil’s works, because they are evil. When you fear the Lord, you will also fear the devil’s works. You will not do them but will stay far away from them.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: fear the works of the devil, for they are evil
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: fear the devil’s works, because they are evil
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The devil’s works themselves are evil and are the object of fear.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The wording is natural while retaining the object of fear identified by the review.

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Fear of the Lord leads to fear of the devil’s works.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The recast states the relationship clearly without narrowing it to a hypothetical condition.

simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: will stay far away from them
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The reader will actively avoid the devil’s works.
simplification_decisions.rationale: Common wording preserves the force of deliberate separation.

risk_flags.risk: “When” may sound temporal rather than express the means indicated by “by fearing.”
risk_flags.mitigation: The sentence sequence still clearly presents fear of the Lord as leading to fear of the devil’s works.

spob_revision_history.previous_text: 3. But be afraid of doing the devil’s evil works. If you fear the Lord, you will also fear such works. You will not do them but will stay far away from them.
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft is generally clear and rightly connects fear of the Lord with refusing the devil’s works. However, its first sentence narrows the warning by making the object “doing” the works rather than the works themselves. Retain the original object while using plain language; the final sentence already makes the practical refusal explicit.

base_translation.text: 4. Therefore there are two fears: if you wish to do what is evil, fear the Lord and you will not do it; and if, on the other hand, you wish to do what is good, fear the Lord and you will do it. Thus the fear of the Lord is strong and great and glorious. So fear the Lord, and you will live to him; and all who fear him, among those who keep his commandments, will live to God.

translation.text: 4. So fear works in two ways. If you want to do evil, fear the Lord, and you will not do it. If you want to do good, fear the Lord, and you will do it. Therefore, the fear of the Lord is powerful, great, and glorious. Fear the Lord, and you will live for him. Everyone who fears him and keeps his commandments will live for God.

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Fear of the Lord both restrains evil and leads to good.
simplification_decisions.rationale: This avoids implying two different objects of fear while preserving the two effects described.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: if, on the other hand, you wish to do what is good
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: If you want to do good
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The second case contrasts choosing good with choosing evil.
simplification_decisions.rationale: The shorter clause states the same contrast in ordinary English.

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: The person's life is directed toward God.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Live for him” clearly expresses the relational direction of the difficult phrase.

risk_flags.risk: “Fear works in two ways” interprets “two fears” as two effects of fearing the Lord.
risk_flags.mitigation: The following parallel clauses explicitly identify both effects.

risk_flags.risk: “Live for him” may sound more purpose-oriented than the unusual phrase “live to him.”
risk_flags.mitigation: The wording retains the central idea of a life directed toward God.

translation.text:
5. I asked, “Sir, why did you say that those who obey his commands ‘will live with God’?”

He answered, “All creation fears the Lord, but it does not obey his commands. Those who fear him and obey his commands have life with God. But those who do not obey his commands have no life in them at all.”

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Their life is with God, as the passage itself explains.
simplification_decisions.reasoning_layer_used: POB translation and immediate explanatory restatement
simplification_decisions.rationale: “With God” avoids wrongly suggesting that they live in service to God.

simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: They do what God commands rather than merely knowing his commands.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “Obey” expresses the intended action in natural modern English.

simplification_decisions.pob_phrase: there is not even life in them
simplification_decisions.simplified_phrase: have no life in them at all
simplification_decisions.preserved_meaning: Those who disobey are described as utterly lacking life.
simplification_decisions.rationale: “At all” naturally preserves the emphatic negative.

interpretive_expansions.claim: The expression describes life with God rather than living for his service or benefit.
evidence: The following explanation says that their life “is with God.”

risk_flags.risk: “Live with God” makes the relational sense more explicit than the quoted POB phrase alone.
risk_flags.mitigation: The passage’s own explanation explicitly states that their life is with God.

spob_revision_history.previous_text:
5. I asked, “Sir, why did you say that those who obey his commands ‘will live for God’?”

He answered, “All creation fears the Lord, but it does not obey his commands. Those who fear him and obey his commands have life with God. But those who do not obey his commands have no life in them at all.”
spob_revision_history.review_summary: The draft successfully makes “keep his commandments” natural and explicit as “obey his commands,” and its final emphatic wording preserves the force of “not even life.” However, “live for God” introduces a potentially different service-oriented sense at the key quoted phrase. The immediate explanation in the passage warrants clarifying the phrase as “live with God,” which is both clearer and aligned with the text’s stated contrast.
